title: What should I do immediately after arriving in Latvia as an international student?
shortAnswer: Complete your university registration, move into accommodation and activate essential services.
answer: After arriving in Latvia, international students should complete university registration, move into their dormitory or apartment, obtain a local SIM card if needed, understand their residence requirements, and familiarize themselves with nearby grocery stores, public transport and healthcare facilities.
tips: Keep your passport and university documents easily accessible during your first week.

title: Do universities organize orientation programs?
shortAnswer: Most universities organize orientation events for new students.
answer: Orientation programs introduce students to the campus, academic system, university services, student organizations and everyday life in Latvia.
tips: Attend orientation to meet other international students.

title: Is English widely spoken at universities?
shortAnswer: Yes, especially in international study programs.
answer: Most international degree programs are taught in English. Administrative staff and international offices also commonly communicate in English.
tips: Learning basic Latvian phrases is still helpful for daily life.

title: Should I learn Latvian?
shortAnswer: It is recommended even if your program is in English.
answer: Knowing basic Latvian makes shopping, public services and daily communication easier. Many universities also offer introductory Latvian language courses.
tips: Learn greetings, numbers and common phrases first.

title: How can I meet other students?
shortAnswer: Join university clubs, events and student organizations.
answer: Most universities have student associations, sports clubs and international communities that organize social events throughout the year.
tips: Participate in welcome events during your first month.

title: Are libraries free for students?
shortAnswer: Yes, enrolled students can generally use university libraries.
answer: University libraries provide study spaces, computers, Wi-Fi and access to books and academic resources.
tips: Carry your student ID when visiting the library.

title: Is Wi-Fi available on campus?
shortAnswer: Yes.
answer: Most Latvian universities provide free Wi-Fi access for enrolled students throughout campus buildings.
tips: Ask your university IT department for login instructions.

title: Can international students work while studying?
shortAnswer: Employment rules depend on your residence status and applicable regulations.
answer: International students should always verify current employment rules through official immigration and university guidance before accepting work.
tips: Confirm legal work conditions before signing an employment contract.

officialSources.name: Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs

title: What documents should I always carry?
shortAnswer: Carry identification and your residence documents when appropriate.
answer: Students should keep important identification documents secure and carry them when required for official purposes.
tips: Store digital copies securely as a backup.

title: What is the most important advice for new international students?
shortAnswer: Complete official paperwork early and actively participate in university life.
answer: Attend orientation, finish all required registrations, learn basic Latvian phrases, understand public transport and begin building your social network during the first few weeks.
tips: The first month is the best time to build friendships.

title: How do I get my student ID card?
shortAnswer: Your university issues it after enrollment.
answer: After completing enrollment, your university will provide instructions for obtaining your student identification card. It is required for accessing many university services.
tips: Carry your student ID whenever you are on campus.

title: What is an ISIC card?
shortAnswer: It is an international student identity card offering various discounts.
answer: Many students use the ISIC card to receive discounts on transportation, museums, restaurants and other services.
tips: Check available ISIC offers regularly.

title: Can international students stay in university dormitories?
shortAnswer: Yes, many universities provide student accommodation.
answer: Dormitory availability depends on the university and room availability. Apply as early as possible.
tips: Reserve your room before arriving in Latvia.

title: What should I bring to my dormitory?
shortAnswer: Bring personal essentials and important documents.
answer: Most students bring bedding if required, toiletries, study materials, chargers, medications and important identification documents.
tips: Ask your dormitory what is already provided.

title: Can I cook in student dormitories?
shortAnswer: Most dormitories provide shared kitchens.
answer: Kitchen facilities vary between dormitories. Follow kitchen rules and clean the area after use.
tips: Label your food if using a shared refrigerator.

title: Can I receive parcels at my dormitory?
shortAnswer: Usually yes.
answer: Most dormitories accept parcels for residents, although procedures differ between universities.
tips: Confirm delivery instructions with your dormitory administration.

title: Can I invite friends to my dormitory?
shortAnswer: Visitor rules depend on your dormitory.
answer: Many student residences allow visitors during specified hours. Always follow dormitory regulations.
tips: Respect quiet hours and visitor policies.

title: Is laundry available in student dormitories?
shortAnswer: Most dormitories provide laundry facilities.
answer: Laundry rooms are commonly available for residents. Some require payment or booking.
tips: Keep detergent available in your room.

title: Is campus Wi-Fi free?
shortAnswer: Yes, universities generally provide free Wi-Fi.
answer: Students receive access credentials after enrollment and can use Wi-Fi in classrooms, libraries and many campus buildings.
tips: Change your password regularly if required by your university.

title: What should I do during my first week at university?
shortAnswer: Attend orientation, explore campus and complete all registrations.
answer: Use your first week to attend orientation events, learn your class locations, activate student services, meet classmates and understand your timetable.
tips: Walk around campus before your first classes begin.

title: Can I open a bank account as an international student?
shortAnswer: Yes, if you meet the bank's identification and residency requirements.
answer: Many Latvian banks offer accounts for international students. Requirements may include your passport, residence permit or visa, proof of address and university enrollment documents.
tips: Compare account fees before choosing a bank.

title: Should I get a Latvian SIM card?
shortAnswer: Yes, it makes communication and online services much easier.
answer: A local SIM card provides affordable mobile data, local phone numbers and easier access to banking and delivery services.
tips: Bring your passport when purchasing a SIM card.

title: Which mobile operators are available in Latvia?
shortAnswer: Latvia has several major mobile network providers.
answer: Students can choose among multiple mobile operators offering prepaid and contract plans depending on their needs.
tips: Compare data plans before purchasing.

title: Can I pay using my international debit or credit card?
shortAnswer: Yes, international cards are widely accepted.
answer: Visa and Mastercard are commonly accepted in shops, restaurants and supermarkets throughout Latvia.
tips: Keep a small amount of cash for emergencies.

title: Where should students buy groceries?
shortAnswer: Latvia has many supermarkets located near residential areas.
answer: Large supermarket chains and neighborhood grocery stores are available throughout Riga and other cities.
tips: Store loyalty cards can reduce grocery expenses.

title: Is Latvia expensive for international students?
shortAnswer: Living costs depend on your lifestyle and city.
answer: Accommodation, transportation and food usually make up the largest monthly expenses. Careful budgeting can help reduce costs.
tips: Track your monthly spending during the first semester.

title: Can I receive money from my home country?
shortAnswer: Yes.
answer: Students can receive international bank transfers and other supported payment methods depending on their financial institution.
tips: Check exchange rates and transfer fees.

title: Can international students use healthcare services?
shortAnswer: Access depends on insurance and residence status.
answer: Healthcare access varies according to insurance coverage and applicable regulations. Universities can provide guidance for international students.
tips: Carry your health insurance information with you.

title: Where can I buy medicines?
shortAnswer: Medicines are available from licensed pharmacies.
answer: Prescription medicines require a valid prescription, while many common medicines are available over the counter.
tips: Look for pharmacies marked with the green pharmacy symbol.

title: What emergency number should every student know?
shortAnswer: Call 112 for emergencies.
answer: Emergency number 112 connects callers to emergency services throughout Latvia, including police, ambulance and fire services.
tips: Save emergency numbers in your phone immediately after arrival.

title: Can I work part-time while studying in Latvia?
shortAnswer: International students may be allowed to work depending on their residence permit conditions.
answer: Employment rights depend on your residence permit, visa type and current immigration regulations. Always verify your eligibility before accepting employment.
tips: Confirm your work rights with the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs.

title: Where can students find part-time jobs?
shortAnswer: Universities, online job portals and local businesses are common sources.
answer: Many students find work through university career centers, online recruitment websites and local employers looking for part-time staff.
tips: Prepare a professional CV before applying.

title: Should I create a Latvian-style CV?
shortAnswer: Yes.
answer: Employers generally expect a professional CV highlighting your education, experience, technical skills and language abilities.
tips: Keep your CV concise and up to date.

title: Can I do internships while studying?
shortAnswer: Many universities encourage internships.
answer: Internships help students gain practical experience and may be integrated into some study programs.
tips: Start applying several months before your preferred internship period.

title: How are university exams conducted?
shortAnswer: Exam formats depend on the course and instructor.
answer: Courses may include written exams, oral examinations, presentations, laboratory work, projects or continuous assessment.
tips: Read the course syllabus carefully at the beginning of the semester.

title: What is plagiarism?
shortAnswer: Presenting someone else's work as your own.
answer: Universities take plagiarism seriously. Always cite your sources correctly and follow your institution's academic integrity policies.
tips: Use proper citations in reports and research papers.

title: Can professors be addressed by their first name?
shortAnswer: Follow your university's academic culture.
answer: When unsure, address professors formally until they indicate another preference.
tips: Professional communication creates a good first impression.

title: How important is class attendance?
shortAnswer: Attendance requirements vary by course.
answer: Some courses require mandatory attendance while others evaluate students mainly through assignments and examinations.
tips: Check attendance rules in every course syllabus.

title: Can students access university sports facilities?
shortAnswer: Many universities provide sports facilities for students.
answer: Universities often offer gyms, sports halls, fitness classes and recreational activities for enrolled students.
tips: Ask your student union about available sports clubs.

title: How can I improve my English and Latvian while studying?
shortAnswer: Practice daily and participate in university activities.
answer: Speaking with classmates, joining student organizations and attending language courses are effective ways to improve communication skills.
tips: Try learning a few new Latvian words every day.

title: How can I make friends in Latvia?
shortAnswer: Join student organizations, university events and international communities.
answer: Most universities organize social events, cultural evenings, sports activities and student clubs where international students can meet classmates and build friendships.
tips: Attend welcome events during your first month.

title: Is Latvia safe for international students?
shortAnswer: Latvia is generally considered a safe country for students.
answer: Students should still follow normal safety precautions, protect personal belongings and avoid isolated areas late at night.
tips: Save emergency number 112 on your phone.

title: Can I travel to other Schengen countries while studying in Latvia?
shortAnswer: Travel depends on your visa or residence permit conditions.
answer: Students should always verify travel requirements and carry valid travel documents before visiting another Schengen country.
tips: Always carry your passport and residence permit when travelling.

title: What clothes should I bring to Latvia?
shortAnswer: Bring clothing suitable for all four seasons, especially warm winter clothing.
answer: Latvia experiences cold winters and mild summers. A warm jacket, waterproof shoes, gloves, scarf and winter hat are highly recommended.
tips: Layered clothing works best during changing seasons.

officialSources.name: Latvian Environment, Geology and Meteorology Centre

title: Does it snow in Latvia?
shortAnswer: Yes, snowfall is common during winter.
answer: Snow usually occurs during the winter season, although conditions vary each year depending on the weather.
tips: Buy waterproof winter footwear before heavy snowfall.

officialSources.name: Latvian Environment, Geology and Meteorology Centre

title: Can I drink tap water in Latvia?
shortAnswer: Tap water is generally safe to drink in Latvia.
answer: Municipal tap water meets drinking water standards in most areas, although some people prefer filtered water based on personal taste.
tips: Carry a reusable water bottle to save money.

title: What is the currency used in Latvia?
shortAnswer: Latvia uses the Euro (€).
answer: All official payments in Latvia are made in Euros. International bank cards are widely accepted.
tips: Most shops accept card payments.

title: Should I carry cash in Latvia?
shortAnswer: A small amount of cash is useful, but cards are widely accepted.
answer: Most businesses accept card payments, although carrying a small amount of cash can be useful for emergencies or small purchases.
tips: Avoid carrying large amounts of cash.

title: How can I manage my monthly student budget?
shortAnswer: Track expenses and prioritize essential spending.
answer: Create a monthly budget covering accommodation, food, transport, study materials and personal expenses. Reviewing spending regularly helps avoid financial stress.
tips: Use a budgeting app to monitor your spending.

title: What is the best advice for succeeding as an international student in Latvia?
shortAnswer: Stay organized, ask questions and actively participate in university life.
answer: Successful students attend classes regularly, communicate with professors, complete assignments on time, participate in campus activities and maintain a healthy balance between studies and personal life.
tips: Don't hesitate to ask your university's international office for help whenever needed.
